sources.title: A One-Sentence Proof That Every Prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) Is a Sum of Two Squares
sources.summary: Two involutions on a finite set turn a parity argument into a representation of a prime by two squares.

sources.title: A simple proof that π is irrational
sources.summary: An auxiliary integral has an integer value under the rationality assumption, while positivity and a factorial bound force it between zero and one.
sources.dependency_review: The one-page proof is self-contained relative to elementary calculus and arithmetic. It has no reference list; no strict source dependency identified.

sources.title: A combinatorial problem in geometry
sources.summary: Convex subsets are extracted from large point configurations through finite colorings, recurrence bounds, and ordered geometric chains.
sources.dependency_review: Ramsey's argument is reproved. König's lemma is a background alternative. An introductory numerical attribution to Makai is catalogued as historical, not used by either proof. No strict dependency established; attribution-only claims are not being certified.

sources.title: Rental Harmony: Sperner's Lemma in Fair Division
sources.summary: Labelled simplicial partitions encode people's choices; refinement and a compactness argument produce compatible allocations of cake, chores, or rooms and rent.
sources.dependency_review: Sperner's lemma is proved in the article. Barycentric subdivision is textbook background. Simmons's private communication is historical credit for a reproduced argument, not an unproved imported fact. No strict source dependency identified for the scoped arguments.

sources.title: An elementary proof of the strong law of large numbers
sources.summary: Truncation and geometric subsequences yield almost-sure averaging under pairwise independence. Later remarks extend the approach to arrays and vector-valued variables.
sources.dependency_review: Scalar proofs use standard probability results. The un-ingested Banach-space remark points to Padgett–Taylor; that is a textbook rather than a strict unique-source dependency. Converse remarks remain outside the current scope.
